name: Keo cu do
summary: Kẹo cu đơ is the peanut candy the city introduction pairs with nước chè xanh. The city introduction traces the name to Cu Hai of Hương Sơn, who sold the candy at a green-tea stall in the first evacuation and put bánh tráng under the peanut brittle so you would not peel a paper off it. The city introduction still calls the pairing the taste of thành Vinh.
origin: The city introduction lists it under Vinh specialties and places the maker in Hương Sơn. Both stay.
history: The city introduction says Cu Hai was nicknamed Cu Đơ because deux is two in French, a joke on Governor Decoux. He was from Hương Sơn and set the candy on bánh tráng instead of a paper you had to peel. Other stalls copied it, and the name stayed.
howToEat: Eat it with the green tea. The city introduction names the sweetness of the candy, the smell and the sharp-sweet tea, and the peanut. It does not print a price or a stall. A price is Check on arrival.
where: With the tea, not a separate address. A street was not printed. Check on arrival.
